notes: The catalogue has no ADXL3xx entry; the closest catalogue type adxl335 (ports ST, Z, Y, X, GND, VCC) was used for the breakout board. The picture's VDD pin is mapped to VCC.
Wiring follows the breadboard image and the pin table, which are the authority. Z goes to A1, Y to A2, X to A3. The schematic draws the X/Y/Z lines crossed, which does not match them.

The breakout's six pins sit in breadboard columns 4-9. The exact columns and rows were read from the image. The module is placed in row e and each jumper in row d of the same column strip, so each wire shares a strip with its pin.

Power comes from A5 (set HIGH, acting as D19) and ground from A4 (set LOW, acting as D18), as in the sketch. The ADXL335 is a 3.3 V part and may be damaged by 5 V, as the tutorial warns. The tutorial says the self-test pin can be left unconnected when the module is powered from 5V and GND. The original circuit connects it to A0, so that wire is kept.
The tutorial does not give wire colours as part properties. The colours are taken from the image.

The manual offers two alternative sensor circuits (potentiometer or 10k photoresistor + 10k resistor divider). I built the first, potentiometer circuit (outer pins to GND and 5V, wiper to A0); the photoresistor variant was not built.

The optional external LED circuit (pin 13 -> 220 ohm resistor -> red LED anode, cathode -> GND next to pin 13) is included, placed on the breadboard in columns 20-25 with two jumper wires; the built-in LED on pin 13 can be used instead. GND.3 is assumed to be the GND pin beside pin 13.

In the potentiometer image the yellow wire appears to end at the far side of the board gap above the pot body; electrically it must reach the pot's middle (wiper) pin, so it is placed in the same strip (11t) as the middle leg.
The potentiometer legs sit in row e of columns 10-12 (GND, SIG, VCC); black and red wires are in row d of columns 10 and 12 (breadboard half nearest the bottom of the image mapped to bank 't').
All parts exist in the catalogue, so no lookup or new part types were needed.
Breadboard rows follow the catalogue naming (bank 'b' = rows f-j, bank 't' = rows a-e). The image labels the half holding the LED and resistor as rows f-j, so that half is bank 'b'.
Column positions were estimated from the image: resistor 3b.g to 6b.g, LED anode 6b.i and cathode 8b.i, pot wiper 23b.f, pot outer pins 22t.e (GND) and 24t.e (5V).
The LED anode is the bent leg, joined to the resistor at column 6. The cathode goes to Uno GND through the black wire at column 8, as the text says.
The Uno has two black GND wires. The one on the digital header (next to AREF) is GND.1. The one on the power header is GND.2.
The potentiometer is the 3-pin trimmer type. Its wiper (SIG) goes to A0, and its outer pins go to 5V and GND.
The 220 ohm resistor sits in series between pin 9 and the LED anode.
Exact breadboard columns and rows are estimated from the image. The pot sits in the lower half, columns 10-12, row f, with each wire in row h of the same column.
The orange wire appears to end at the top of the pot body in the image. I assumed it connects to the middle (wiper) pin's column, as the text and schematic say.
Outer pins go to GND (black wire) and 5V (red wire). The middle pin goes to A0 (orange wire). The pot is symmetric between GND and VCC, so which outer pin is which does not matter.
The Uno's GND.1 is used for ground. Any Uno GND pin would work.
No LED is used, so no series resistor is needed. The serial output (9600 baud over USB) is software only and is not drawn as a part.

Each LED branch: Mega pin (2-13) -> jumper -> bottom bank column -> 220 ohm resistor across the centre gap -> top bank column -> LED anode; LED cathode goes into the top ground rail (tn), which a black wire ties to Mega GND. Exact breadboard hole positions are simplified from the image (the image routes cathodes via black jumpers) but connectivity matches the schematic.
Copy k of the repeat uses breadboard column k and Mega pin k+1 (pins 2..13).
Mega GND port name assumed to be GND.1, following the catalogue naming of other boards.
Resistors are 220 ohm and LEDs red, per the manual; all catalogue parts, so no new part types.

The manual shows several target/programmer combinations (UNO-UNO, UNO-NANO, MEGA-UNO, MKR1000-UNO). I built the main 'old style wiring' UNO (programmer) to UNO (target) example: D11 to D11 (MOSI), D12 to D12 (MISO), D13 to D13 (SCK), D10 to target RESET, 5V to 5V, GND to GND.

The three optional ArduinoISP status LEDs are included. The manual gives no pins, so I used the ArduinoISP sketch defaults: heartbeat on D9, error on D8, programming on D7. Each has a 220 ohm series resistor to GND via the breadboard ground rail. The resistor value is my assumption.

The 10 uF electrolytic capacitor is placed between the programmer's RESET and GND, with the positive leg on RESET, because the manual says UNO programmers need it. It must be added only after the ArduinoISP sketch has been uploaded.
The USB cable and host computer are not modelled. The manual says not to power the boards while wiring. The target is powered from the programmer's 5V pin.
Only the old-style header wiring is built. The ICSP header alternative is not.
The manual's main example uses the built-in LED; I built the optional external LED circuit that the manual and images describe.

The image labels the breadboard's top half rows j-f. The catalogue's top bank 't' is rows a-e and its bottom bank 'b' is rows f-j. So the circuit, which sits in the image's top half (rows f-j), uses bank 'b' holes.

The LED's bent leg (anode, longer) is in column 6 and its straight leg (cathode) is in column 8. The resistor spans columns 3 and 6 in row h. The orange wire goes from pin 13 to 3b.g. The black wire goes from the GND pin next to pin 13 (GND.1) to 8b.g.
The resistor sits in the same column strip as the LED anode (6b), and the GND wire shares column strip 8b with the LED cathode.
